# Fixture suite coverage map

This file is the census of record for the committed fixture suite: which
dialect constructs, diagnostic codes, and CLI verb contracts the suite
exercises, and which gaps are declared elisions rather than silently
uncovered. The suite itself lives in this directory and runs under the
`kdlith-fixtures` harness (see `README.md`).

## Maintenance rule

The map is hand-maintained, and two invariants keep it honest:

1. Every scenario name written in this file must appear in the output of
   `kdlith-fixtures --fx-list` for the committed suite. A name that names
   no real scenario is a bug in this file.
2. Every non-parse scenario in `--fx-list` output must appear somewhere in
   the census tables below. `parse/kdl-spec` (243 scenarios, one per
   upstream KDL v2 positive case) is covered as a single row: the official
   KDL v2 suite, traced in `parse/kdl-spec/PROVENANCE.md`. The upstream
   negative cases live one-per-scenario under `invalid/kdl-spec/` and are
   named individually in the code census.

Adding or renaming a scenario means updating this file in the same commit.
The census is re-checkable by hand:

```sh
target/debug/kdlith-fixtures --fx-suite tests/fixtures --fx-kdlith target/debug/kdlith --fx-list
```

then diffing the listed names (all except `parse/kdl-spec/*`) against the
scenario names occurring in this file, in both directions. Paths the prose
cites that are not scenarios — committed suite files and directories such
as `parse/kdl-spec/PROVENANCE.md`, `processing/bind/profiles.kdl`, or a
schema directory read by suite path, and the `target/debug` build path —
are citations, not census entries; the reverse direction skips them. If
the census is ever automated, its tokenizer must tell such paths from
scenario names.

Suite state at the time of writing: 1294 scenarios — 243 `parse/kdl-spec`,
1051 others — all green. 43 of them are heavy (the codegen scenarios whose
steps compile a scratch workspace, marked `"heavy": true` in their
manifests): a default harness run excludes them and prints the count it
skipped, and they run deliberately through `--fx-heavy` or an explicit
`--fx-filter`; `--fx-list` still lists every scenario.

## Construct census

One row per in-scope mechanism row of the dialect record
(`context.internal/reference/`, mechanism files). "Defining file" is
the canonical dialect document
that declares the mechanism.

The invocation's listed set (`--profiles`, see its row) selects among its members by the same rules: the members whose effective rules match (`profiles-set-rules`), all of them when several match, admitting the union of their effective roots and `profile=` chains (`profiles-set-multi`), else the listed default (`profiles-set-default`), else nothing: an unmatched entry with no listed default is SCH011 (`invalid/data/profiles-set-unmatched`), never the first listed; each invalid twin rejects a node only a non-selected member, or the unlisted schema default, would admit. Rules read the entry path relative to the project root (`--root`, spelled `--match-root` by these scenarios): lexically normalized (`profile-match-normalized`: `./outlet/../outlet/stock.kdl` selects as `outlet/stock.kdl`), relative to `--match-root` (`profile-match-root`, a parent-relative spelling; `profile-match-root-absolute`, an absolute entry under an absolute root, both selecting what a run inside the root selects), and relative to the current directory without one (`invalid/data/profile-match-root-unanchored`: the same tree-prefixed path matches no rule and the default's admission rejects the gadget). The harness runs each scenario in one directory, so the cwd-variation itself is not staged; the absolute arm stands for it. The profile each entry invocation selected is carried per document by the generated typed reader asked for provenance — named, match-selected, and set members in listed order, the import-reached documents included — with an unknown named profile refused before any document is read |

The diagnostic registry (`pkg/rs/diagnostic/src/registry.rs`) is the
census authority: every registered code appears below with an explicit
status — `covered`, `UNCOVERED`, or `elided-with-reason` — even when the
code is absent from the design record's table.

## Harness-protection census

What the suite proves about the harness itself, beyond the processor
under test.

| Protection | Exercised by | State |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Fail-closed scratch classification of a planted violation (symlink and foreign file reported as foreign entries by the harness, link never followed, neither silently deleted) | harness/scratch-fail-closed | covered — doubles as the detection meta-fixture: neutralizing the classification fails the scenario |
| Absence pin: `stdout-not-contains` passes when none of its substrings appears in stdout | harness/stdout-not-contains | covered — the help output carries the verb tree and none of the create, update, delete, or promote lifecycle commands |
| Absence pin detection: `stdout-not-contains` fails a run whose stdout carries a forbidden substring, in a positive `expect` and in a codegen-oracle `exercise` step | harness/stdout-not-contains-detects | covered — the detection meta-fixture: the scenario runs the harness itself over its committed inner suite, whose two scenarios each forbid a substring their run prints, and requires the inner run to exit 1 with exactly those two forbidden-needle failures and no other failure; neutralizing either check level fails the scenario |
| Embedded-equivalence pair: `source-embedded: ["NAME=DIR"]` runs the scenario with `--source NAME=DIR` and again through the `fx-kdlith-embedded` helper with DIR embedded as NAME, and fails on any difference in exit code, stdout, or stderr before judging the expectation against the embedded run | harness/source-embedded-detects, processing/locations/embedded-pair, invalid/data/location-embedded-escape, invalid/data/location-embedded-missing, schemas/vet/import-source-embedded, invalid/schemas/location-named-escape, processing/assets/embedded-pair | covered — the detection meta-fixture runs before any product scenario relies on the pair: it runs the harness itself over its committed inner suite, whose agree scenario passes and whose diverge scenario (a file that is not UTF-8 in the source, so only the helper fails, while the scenario declares the helper's exit 3) must fail on the pair alone, reporting the exit and both streams; the inner run must exit 1 with exactly that failure. The relation is metamorphic: neither run is a snapshot of the other's implementation, and the harness compares them itself |

An indented line after a brace-less node is therefore a sibling, never a child: it parses clean (`sibling-lines`) and binds at its real position, so a would-be child is rejected unbound under the root (`indented-line-not-child`, BND001), never silently bound into the preceding node, with a note asking whether it was meant to nest there (`processing/bnd001-sibling-hint`). Every seeded `state/` is the bytes a real refresh of the scenario's inputs wrote (the `source-*` states then carry the canary), pinned unchanged after the read. | `gen` generated-crate diagnostic rendering (the re-exported `DiagnosticRecord`'s shared `render` presentation) | codegen/gen-schema-render-diagnostic | covered — a consumer depending on the generated crate alone renders the reading's binding diagnostic through the re-exported `DiagnosticRecord::render` (the presentation the record type itself owns, which the CLI prints verbatim on every verb), then runs the CLI's `vet data` on the same schema and document and requires the two renderings to be the same bytes before the exercise exits; the harness pins both renderings byte for byte (`error[KDLITH-BND005]:` head, `--> inputs/data.kdl:1:16` location, `help:` correction) and the determinism and compile steps ride the codegen-oracle shape |

## Declared elisions

Each row names a gap the suite deliberately does not exercise, why, and
the condition that reopens it. No scenario anywhere reports an elided
behavior as passed.

| Gap | Why it is not exercised | Reopen condition |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Compile-stage checks after a reader error on the inspect path | `inspect dialect` and `inspect schema` stream every item, then run the same compile-stage checks `vet` runs, and the reader and compile diagnostics decide the exit together; the seven compile-stage `processing/inspect-rejects-*` scenarios (seven directories, not counting the three `inspect-rejects-view-*` stream-view pins; earlier prose counted six fault kinds, two of them sharing DLC006) and the four single-file `dialect/canonical-inspect/*` scenarios pin that rejection. When the reader itself reports an error, the compile stage is skipped, because the loader re-reads the same documents and stops on those errors: such a run reports only the reader diagnostics, and nothing about the input was compile-checked, so a compile-only fault in the same input stays unreported until the reader faults are fixed | The loader can compile past reader errors without repeating them — add an inspect scenario carrying both a reader fault and a compile-only fault |
| Import namespace visibility gating in generated processors — closed by fixture | Decision: closed. A generated processor's linked reading runs the engine's link stage, which gates under the namespace, and the typed oracle (`codegen/gen-schema-reference-type/linking`) pins both ends inside the generated crate: a document imported under a namespace resolves its own unqualified name with an empty gated list, while sibling documents' links to the same name carry the namespace in their gated list, each line derived from `vet data` and `inspect data --view references` on the same inputs; the CLI-side positive and negative ends are pinned by `processing/linking/namespace-self`, `processing/linking/references-namespace-self`, and `invalid/data/reference-namespace-sibling`. Every generated-processor resolution fixture resolves through a linked reading; the library offers no name-only resolution path | None |
| Snapshot restore surface (KDLITH-CTX004) — closed by fixture | Decision: closed. `read data --state` restores a record from its snapshot, and the restore's fingerprint and lineage checks are reached end to end from real seeds: `invalid/data/read-entry-snapshot-fingerprint-mismatch` and `invalid/data/read-entry-snapshot-lineage-mismatch` pin KDLITH-CTX004, and `processing/read-data-entry-restore` with its byte-identical twin `processing/read-data-entry-restore-replay` pins the restore itself (see the `read data --state` row) | Not elided |
| Slot layers through context snapshots — closed by fixture | Decision: closed. `processing/read-data-entry-restore-layered` and its byte-identical twin `processing/read-data-entry-restore-layered-replay` restore a record whose layered slot holds an override-layer value, and a base-layer set inside the record's own span is outranked by it; a restore that dropped the layer or restored it as base makes that set KDLITH-CTX006 and fails the golden (both mutations were run). `invalid/data/read-entry-snapshot-layered-fingerprint-mismatch` pins the layered snapshot's CTX004 | Not elided |
| KDLITH-CTX006 raised after a snapshot restore | Justified, not deferred: two invariants make it unreachable from a real seed. `cache refresh` writes nothing when the reading reports an error diagnostic, and a snapshot's key carries the record document's revision, so a record whose own span repeats a layer fails the scan and no snapshot of those exact inputs can exist; a changed document misses the key and replays. A hand-minted seed would be the only way to raise it. The same-layer arm is pinned on the live path by `invalid/data/slot-layered-same-layer` | A snapshot that can be written while its record reports an error, or one keyed without the record document's revision |
| Restoring a record an import reached | `read data --state` restores records bound from the record document's own text; a record an import of that document bound carries another document's revision in its index entry, and the read locates spans only in the document it names, so such a record is a miss and replays (its output is the replay's by construction) | The read locates an indexed record's span in the imported document the index entry names |
| Reference linking outside the declared reference surface and the vet/inspect data and export verbs | `vet data`, `inspect data`, and `export` link only references a declared reference type looks up (each code pinned in the code census; export's scope gate pinned by `processing/export/scope-local-unresolved` and `invalid/export/unresolved-reference-complete`); plain `ref<T>` values keep their own mechanisms (inline dependent-binding validation, the contribution resolver's `follows` policy pinned by `processing/resolution/missing-allow`) and never fail a run as REF001. `read data`, `list items`, and `cache refresh` do not link, so `read data --entry` composition is pinned via the source index rather than resolution. A generated reader links a collected reading through the same link stage (`codegen/gen-schema-reference-type/linking` pins every outcome and diagnostic against the CLI, and `codegen/gen-schema-ref-import` resolves the catalog schema's declared reference type through it, a missing target failing KDLITH-REF001 and a name declared twice resolving to the first declaration beside KDLITH-REF002) | Another data verb links a reading, or a generated reader links on a path other than a collected reading — add its resolution negatives and tighten `processing/read-data-entry` |
| Undeclared match target (`KDLITH-SCH006`) | A match rule carries only its TEXT and binds only as a child of the `match` block inside the profile it selects (`path-suffix|path-prefix|file-name TEXT` under `match` under `profile`), so a rule's target is always its enclosing, declared profile: no surface spelling names a match target, and an undeclared one cannot be written. The nearest reachable spellings are pinned instead — a `match` block outside any profile is unbound (`invalid/schemas/profile-match-outside-profile`, KDLITH-BND001), and an undeclared `extends` is SCH006 (`invalid/schemas/profile-extends-undeclared`) | The dialect gains a match-rule form that names its target profile (a target property or a schema-level rule list) — add its undeclared-target SCH006 negative |
| KDLITH-SRC003 byte-size arms | A document or `--resolve-from` file over 16 MiB, a token over 8 MiB, a source over 4 GiB, and a multi-line string over one million lines are each refused before allocation, but provoking one means committing (or generating at run time, which the scenario format cannot do) an input of that size; a fixture tens of megabytes large is a repository cost out of proportion to a size comparison. Every structural limit arm — parser depth, comment depth, binding depth, import depth, import count — is pinned instead, each with its message | The scenario format gains a generated-input step, or the limits become configurable from the CLI so a small input can cross a lowered limit |
| KDLITH-SCH005 per-reason arms beyond the design record's three | The compiler words about fifteen reasons under SCH005 (a field without a source, a field type redundant with or missing beside `type=`, `duplicate-keys` without a keyed source, alternative sources without a collision policy, a context source without a policy, a children rule permitting no occurrence, a descendant or sequence naming no declared or permitted node, malformed sequence steps, a field name outside the identifier form). The design record states the code's contract as three kinds — an unconsumed argument, contradictory child rules, and groups — and each kind is pinned; the remaining reasons are the same code under the same contract, and pinning the wording of each would freeze message text the record does not promise | The design record names a further SCH005 kind, or a reason moves to its own code |
| `inspect data --view references` writes no report when a read stops | The design record states both arms: a syntax fault, a missing document, or a crossed limit completes the reading as diagnostics and the report prints with the links bound before the fault (each reachable arm was run, exit 1), while a reading the reader abandons as broken writes none. That abandoned branch (`ReadError`) is reached only by an event-source contract break, an unknown item kind, or a capture of an undeclared slot, none of which a CLI input provokes, so no scenario can drive it | A CLI input stops the reader |
| `inspect data` stream views over a `--schema` that does not compile | The design record says the stream views, `context`, and `references` write nothing and exit 1 when the `--schema` schema does not compile. The rule is one branch shared by every data view — the schema load fails before any reading exists — and `processing/inspect-view-plan-data-compile-failed` pins it through `plan`; the other six views take the same branch (each was run: empty stdout, the load diagnostic only, exit 1) | A data view renders before the schema load decides |
| Reference keys of a declared generic map type | A field typed by an instantiation of a declared generic type (`T<A, B>`, such as a declared map type keyed by a reference type) is walked neither by the plan's deferred list nor by the link stage's field typing: both stop at an instantiation, so neither names a reference type held in its arguments. `processing/inspect-view-plan-reference-type` pins the shapes the plan walks | A declared generic map type's key references need link-stage typing or plan visibility — extend both walkers together and add a plan-view and a link scenario for that field |
| Linked-reading resolution in `codegen/gen-schema-ref-import` — closed by fixture | Decision: closed. The catalog schema declares the name-only reference type `GroupRef` and its entry's group field is typed by it, so the link stage links every group reference; the exercise collects its data as a reading linked under complete scope and resolves each reference through `Reading::resolve`, which answers `Resolved::Declaration` or — for a reference the open-world arm admitted, as `codegen/gen-schema-openworld` proves over the open-world schema — `Resolved::External` at the site with no default value; the former library-level name-only index is removed. The earlier name-only ambiguous outcome for a name declared twice is not a link-stage outcome: the link stage keeps the first declaration of an identity and reports the second as a duplicate (KDLITH-REF002), so the reference resolves; ambiguity stays pinned by `processing/linking/references-ambiguous` and `codegen/gen-schema-reference-type/linking` | None |
| Committed run commands name the `target/debug` build path | The committed commands are the contract; on hosts where that build path is unavailable a host-local substitution runs the same binaries | None — host note only |
| In-memory definition loading in the reference processor and the dialect form (`load_dialect_sources`, `load_schema_sources`, `load_schema_sources_with`) | The loaders are library entry points beside the path loaders: they read `Source` documents through the same typed reader and compiler, and an unprefixed import inside an in-memory definition fails closed (KDLITH-LOC001), since a document held in memory belongs to no source. Every definition verb loads from paths, so no CLI scenario reaches them; `codegen/gen-dialect-oracle` pins that the generated dialect processor emits the same loaders byte for byte, and `codegen/gen-schema-source-reexport` exercises the schema form's `load_sources`/`load_sources_with`, which call `load_schema_sources_with` | A codegen-oracle exercise drives the dialect form's loaders, or a CLI verb loads definitions from memory |

## Story checklist

The acceptance criteria this suite answers to, with their gate commands:

- [ ] `cargo build --workspace` exits 0 (run unpiped; record the literal exit code)
- [ ] The repository's lint gate exits 0 (run unpiped; record the literal exit code)
- [ ] `/usr/bin/rg --no-ignore --hidden -n 'cfg\(test\)|#\[test\]' pkg tools tests --glob '*.rs'` returns zero matches
- [ ] `target/debug/kdlith-fixtures --fx-suite tests/fixtures --fx-kdlith target/debug/kdlith` exits 0 unpiped, with all counts recorded (the default run skips the heavy scenarios and prints how many)
- [ ] `target/debug/kdlith-fixtures --fx-suite tests/fixtures --fx-kdlith target/debug/kdlith --fx-heavy` exits 0 unpiped, with all counts recorded (every scenario, heavy ones included)
- [ ] Each commit subject is conventional, lowercase, at most 72 characters, with no body (`git log --format=%s%n%b`)
- [ ] The codegen-oracle scenario kind runs the full generate → compare → compile → exercise chain over `pkg/kdl/dialect.kdl` (`codegen/gen-dialect-oracle`, a heavy scenario: it runs under `--fx-heavy` or an explicit `--fx-filter`, and a gate that does not run it says so); no other declared elision names the codegen surface
- [ ] Every `tests/fixtures/invalid/` scenario carries an `expect-invalid` code line, except a gen refusal, whose one line prints no registered code (see the GEN004 row): those pin the refusal line itself with exit 1 (`invalid/schemas/no-reading-nodes`, `invalid/codegen/recursive-type/*`)
